model.name: Zoom-out always grows the SVG diagram canvas (fixes the space problem) with per-diagram persisted zoom where 1 = 100% = whole diagram
model.description: Tron item-1 (HIGHEST PRI, acute 'space problem'). Zooming OUT is ALWAYS possible and GROWS the SVG diagram canvas so more elements fit; the zoom level is SAVED on the Diagram unit (persisted per-diagram); zoom level 1 = 100% = frames the WHOLE diagram, and stays anchored so 1 always frames the whole diagram as it grows. Reuse RbPanZoom (already used for R33.6.2 edge-autoscroll), NO fork.
model.tronQuote: > TRON (2026-07-31): adding more elements ends up in a space problem; zooming OUT is always possible and increases the size of the SVG diagram; the zoom level is saved on the diagram; 1 = 100% = see the whole diagram.

discoverySource.note: Tron item-1: zoom-out grows SVG canvas + per-diagram persisted zoom (1=whole). Highest pri (space problem). Reuse RbPanZoom.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Zooming OUT is ALWAYS available and GROWS the SVG diagram canvas (more room for elements) - never blocked/clamped-to-a-floor that traps the user in a full canvas. Reuses RbPanZoom.
The current zoom level is PERSISTED on the Diagram unit (per-diagram, MODEL_STORE) and SURVIVES a reload / fresh re-mount - reopening the diagram restores its saved zoom.
Zoom level 1 = 100% = frames the WHOLE diagram; as the canvas grows via zoom-out, level 1 stays anchored to frame the whole diagram (1 is always 'fit whole').

GATE @390 (screenshot/pixel + planted bite): on a crowded diagram, zoom OUT -> canvas grows + elements fit (space problem solved); reload -> the saved zoom level is restored; set to 1 -> the whole diagram is framed. planted: zoom-out blocked or zoom not persisted = RED.

model.designAdopted: Adopted design 8aa19d090: AC-zoom-out-grows-canvas+AC-zoom-1-is-whole <- INV-Z1 (RbPanZoom MIN 0.25+clamp-center+viewBox pad, setScale seam); AC-zoom-persist-on-diagram <- INV-Z2 (POST /api/model/diagram/zoom store-only, client setScale init). 2 chains: client zoom-range + server persist. Names provisional.
